# ADR-0002: Apply approved-list changes by restarting rqlited one node at a time

> **Status:** accepted | **Date:** 2026-11-21

**References:** [RFC-0001:C-APPROVED-LIST-TRUST](../rfc/RFC-0001.md#rfc-0001c-approved-list-trust), [RFC-0001:C-APPROVED-LIST-BLOCK](../rfc/RFC-0001.md#rfc-0001c-approved-list-block), [RFC-0001:C-MTLS](../rfc/RFC-0001.md#rfc-0001c-mtls)

## Context

Under approved-list trust, every node must accept exactly the approved certificates once a change is applied, offline, without making a Location with more than one voter lose its majority. The rqlite source (master `4452a98`, checked 2026-11-19) shows that the CA file given by `-node-ca-cert` and `-http-ca-cert` is read only at startup (`setCertPool` in `internal/rtls/config.go`), that there is no CRL or OCSP, and that only the node's own certificate and key are reloaded (`internal/rtls/reloader.go`, since 8.37.0).

## Decision

After each approval or block, the Location Agent rebuilds the trust file on each node from the approved list stored in the Location Cluster and restarts `rqlited` one node at a time, the Leader last after transferring leadership. Only one round runs at a time; a change made during a round is applied by a following round.

The next node restarts only after the previous one has rejoined the Location Cluster and caught up with the Leader. Exact timing and how leadership is transferred are left to implementation and checked in the rqlite capabilities tests (roadmap 2.1).

A machine that was off during a change fetches the current list from another approved node before starting `rqlited`. If no approved node can be reached, the agent starts `rqlited` with its last trust file only when the machine was the sole voter at shutdown, since no change can have committed without it. Otherwise it keeps retrying and does not start `rqlited` until it has the current list.

## Consequences

Benefits: works with rqlite as it is today and keeps the majority on Locations with more than one voter.

Costs: every approval or block restarts every node. Each round transfers leadership once, which pauses writes briefly even with more than one voter (hashicorp/raft rejects writes while a leadership transfer is in progress); with a single voter, writes pause for a few seconds during its restart, which is accepted. During a block round, nodes not yet restarted keep accepting the blocked machine's certificate until their turn. The Location Agent must coordinate rounds and their order. A machine that comes back while no other approved node is reachable cannot serve even local reads until it fetches the list.

If rqlite later reloads the CA file without a restart, a new ADR should reconsider this decision; proposing that change upstream is optional and not a dependency.

## Alternatives Considered

### Rebuild the trust file and restart rqlited one node at a time, Leader last (accepted)

- **Pros:** Works with current rqlite, No loss of majority with more than one voter
- **Cons:** Restarts every node on each change, Short write pause with a single voter

### Wait for rqlite to reload the CA file without restarting (rejected)

- **Pros:** No restarts
- **Rejected because:** The feature does not exist; depending on an upstream change would block approved-list trust.
